day_02_morning: ^Dawn comes grey through the ash. The Watch checkpoint at the end of Ember Row is closed.
^Two guards stand behind the barrier. Neither of them looks at you.
^They have been looking at the same spot on the wall for an hour, Iven says. That is not discipline. That is fear.
^I have a ledger with every debt in this district, and a reason to collect.
^The guard glances at the paper. His hand does not move toward his weapon.
^Somewhere beyond the gate, something metal scratches stone.
^That is not a dog, Iven says.
^The barrier lifts six inches. Enough to crawl through. Enough to regret.
^Slip through the ash gate while they argue.
bluff: ^The guard reads a name. Then another. His jaw tightens.
^Elias Voss, Iven says. You know the name. You wrote it down yourself.
^That was either very brave or very stupid, Iven says.
gate: ^You wait until the guards turn toward the sound. Then you are under the barrier and through.
^Iven follows a heartbeat later, cursing under his breath.
^You are going to get us both killed, he says.
day_02_afternoon: ^The Hound finds you between the furnace and the wall. There is no room left to run.
^It is all angles and old iron, a Watch dog built to keep a gate that no longer exists.
^Its eyes are the color of a bell held too close to a flame.
^Elias is behind it. Alive. Bleeding. Trying to say something through the smoke.
^The Hound does not growl. It lowers its head.
^Iven draws. Mara plants her feet. The Bell in your chest rings once, quietly, waiting.
stand: ^Good, Mara says. The Hound is faster than us. So we make it come to the wall.
^You put your back to the iron and wait.
furnace: ^Iven sees the furnace door before you do. He puts a bolt through the hinge.
^The Hound turns toward the sound. The door opens. The heat comes out like a hand.
day_02_night: ^Elias is alive. The Watch will want him back before dawn.
^He sits on the edge of the Spire stair with the ledger open on his knees.
^Every debt in Ember Row, he says. And one I cannot pay.
^You do not ask which one. You already know.
^The Bell hangs above you. The crack has widened by a hair.
^What you keep now will survive the reset. What you owe may not.
keep: ^Elias closes the book. Some debts are only numbers, he says. Some are people.
give: ^Iven takes the ledger like it might bite him. He does not open it.
^I will hold it, he says. Not spend it.
burn: ^The pages curl. The names go up in smoke. Elias watches without a word.
^No one owes anyone now, you say.
^Elias looks at the empty cover for a long time.
